newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-TIGER FAILS BUT STILL IMPRESSES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER FAILS BUT STILL IMPRESSES.

text.p: The massively talented Tiger Woods arrived as the hottest favourite in years to win the British Open but three horrendous holes which saw him post a quadruple and two triple bogeys prevented him from even coming close.
His closing three-over-par 74 left him on 284, 12 shots shy of the winner, fellow American Justin Leonard.
But the experience has not dimmed Woods's desire to capture the British title one day.
"I have always been determined to win the British Open. It is the one with the most tradition. It would mean a lot to me," said the 21-year-old who turned professional just under a year ago.
"I always look forward to coming over here. It is the epitome of being creative. You cannot bump and run on our courses. Here you have to have imagination."
Although he failed to win this time, there can be few who watched him play who doubt he is more than likely to succeed in future years.
His power off the tee is awesome. One immense drive of 435 yards in the opening round drew gasps of disbelief from spectators.
But there is far more to his game than just power. His approach play with delicate chips to the greens matches that of anyone and his accuracy is at times astonishing.

During the third round on Saturday he holed a chip of 30 yards by bouncing the ball deliberately off a slope in front of him. He said he had aimed at a particular spot on the slope but was three inches off. Three inches!
He is a perfectionist. He expects to win -- every time.
A few times on Sunday his exasperation with himself showed as any hope of winning slipped away with missed opportunities.
Although eight behind overnight leader Jesper Parnevik of Sweden at the start of the fourth round, Woods still believed he had a chance of victory.
"When I started out I just tried to be patient and get opportuniities for birdies. I was doing that until I missed two putts," he said.

"At the sixth it was about eight feet and the seventh three feet. If I had made those two putts I might have got going." He swung the club angrily in the direction of the ball after missing the second.
The best of Woods came in the third round when he had a 64 to equal the record round at Troon in a British Open.
That was the only round not to include a damaging, high-scoring hole.

On Sunday, that came at the par-three eighth, titled the Postage Stamp. His tee shot ended in a steep-sided bunker below the level of the raised green and he took two attempts to get out. A long putt went five feet past and he lipped the hole from there before he finally sank it for a six.
"I knew I couldn't win after that," he said.
